ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are five gray squares and two white right triangles in the figure. Outside the two legs of the left right triangle are respectively connected squares labeled with areas 3 and 22, and the other side is connected to the large middle square with no number labeled. The right right triangle is also connected to this middle square, and outside the other two sides are respectively connected squares labeled 8 and a question mark. Reasoning: According to the structure in the figure, the middle square with no number labeled is the square on the hypotenuse of the left right triangle, while the squares with areas 3 and 22 are on the two legs. By the area form of the Pythagorean theorem, area of the hypotenuse square = sum of the areas of the squares on the two legs, so the area of the middle square is 3 + 22 = 25. Now look at the right right triangle: the middle square is the square on its hypotenuse, with area 25; the squares with areas 8 and ? are on the two legs. Therefore 8 + ? = 25, giving ? = 25 - 8 = 17.
